quests.instruction: Blend /s/ /k/ /r/ /a/ /p/. Which word do you get?
quests.hint: Say each sound, then speed up. How many sounds are at the start?
quests.explanation: /s/ /k/ /r/ /a/ /p/ makes “scrap”. “Scrape” has long a and “script” has a different vowel and ending.
quests.funFact: Scrap has five sounds. Short words can still have lots of sounds when they begin with a blend.

quests.instruction: Which word rhymes with “shrink”?
quests.hint: Match the ending sounds, not just the beginning.
quests.explanation: “Shrink” and “blink” share the ending -ink.

quests.instruction: Which word is read /ch/ /e/ /s/ /t/?
quests.hint: Check each sound against the letters.
quests.explanation: “Chest” has four sounds: /ch/ /e/ /s/ /t/. “Cheat” has long e and “chess” has no /t/.

quests.instruction: Change only the vowel in “ship”. Which word do you get?
quests.hint: Keep the /sh/ at the start and the /p/ at the end.
quests.explanation: Changing only the vowel in “ship” gives “shop”. “Chip” changes the first sound and “shin” changes the last.

quests.instruction: Which pair of words differs by only one sound?
quests.hint: Say both words in each pair and compare every sound.
quests.explanation: “Back” and “pack” differ only in their first sound. The other pairs have more differences.
quests.funFact: Words that differ by only one sound are called minimal pairs. They help you hear tiny sound differences.

quests.instruction: Change the second sound in “slip” from /l/ to /n/. Which word do you get?
quests.hint: Keep the /s/ at the start and the /ip/ at the end. Only the middle sound of the blend changes.
quests.explanation: Replacing /l/ with /n/ turns “slip” into “snip”. “Skip” would use /k/ and “ship” would use the digraph /sh/.
quests.funFact: Swapping one sound in a blend gives a whole new word: slip, snip, skip.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? tr__l — a path you walk on in the woods.
quests.hint: The long a is in the middle of the word, followed by a consonant.
quests.explanation: “Trail” spells long a with ai in the middle. The ay spelling is mostly used at the end.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? pl__ — you do this at the park.
quests.hint: This word ends with the long a sound.
quests.explanation: “Play” ends with ay, the usual spelling at the end of a word.

quests.instruction: Which is the correct spelling of the word that means to stay until something happens?
quests.hint: Three spellings can make long a. Which one is right here?
quests.explanation: “Wait” uses ai for long a. Some words just have to be remembered with their spelling.
quests.funFact: Long a has many spellings: ai, ay, a_e and more. Seeing words often helps you remember which one goes with each word.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? b__ch — you play in the sand there.
quests.hint: Both ea and ee make long e. Think of the place you build sandcastles.
quests.explanation: “Beach” is spelled with ea. “Beech” is a different word, a kind of tree.
quests.funFact: Beach and beech sound the same but mean different things.

quests.instruction: Which is the correct spelling of the colour of grass?
quests.hint: Think about the spelling of long e that you see in tree.
quests.explanation: “Green” uses ee for the long e sound.

quests.instruction: Which letters complete the word? w__k — seven days make one.
quests.hint: Think about the meaning. Seven days make one…
quests.explanation: “Week” uses ee. “Weak” sounds the same but means not strong.

quests.instruction: Here is a made-up word: “dib”. Which sounds does it make?
quests.hint: Use the letters you know. Say each sound and blend them.
quests.explanation: “Dib” follows the CVC pattern with short i: /d/ /i/ /b/. Even a made-up word can be read with phonics.
quests.funFact: Made-up words are a good test. If you can read a word you have never seen, you are really decoding.

quests.instruction: Here is a made-up word: “glop”. Which real word rhymes with it?
quests.hint: Look at the ending of glop and match it.
quests.explanation: “Glop” ends with -op, just like “stop”.

quests.instruction: Here is a made-up word: “jate”. Which vowel sound does it have?
quests.hint: Look at the end of the word. Is there a silent e?
quests.explanation: “Jate” has the a_e pattern, so it would be read with long a.

quests.instruction: Which two words have the same consonants but different vowels?
quests.hint: Look at the first and last letters of each word.
quests.explanation: “Bit” and “bat” both start with b and end with t. Only the vowel changes.

quests.instruction: Change the vowel in “sheep” to short i. Which word do you make?
quests.hint: Say sheep, then change just the middle sound.
quests.explanation: “Sheep” becomes “ship” when the vowel changes from long e to short i.

quests.instruction: Remove the silent e from “tape”. Which word do you get?
quests.hint: Take away the last letter and read the new word.
quests.explanation: “Tape” without the e is “tap”, and the vowel changes from long a to short a.
quests.funFact: Adding or removing a silent e can change a short vowel to a long vowel and back again.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same vowel sound as “boat”, but is spelled with a silent e?
quests.hint: Look for the o_e pattern.
quests.explanation: “Boat” and “bone” both have long o. “Boat” uses oa, and “bone” uses o_e.
quests.funFact: Boat and bone have the same vowel sound, spelled in two different ways.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with the same sound as “cage”, but spelled differently?
quests.hint: Listen for the /j/ sound at the end.
quests.explanation: “Cage” ends with /j/ spelled ge. “Edge” ends with /j/ spelled dge.

quests.instruction: Which word has the same vowel sound as “moon”, but is spelled differently?
quests.hint: Say moon and match the vowel.
quests.explanation: “Moon” has oo and “grew” has ew. Both say long oo. “Glow” has long o and “gray” has long a.

quests.instruction: Which word has a silent letter and the long i sound spelled igh?
quests.hint: Look for both clues in one word.
quests.explanation: “Knight” starts with a silent k and has igh for long i. “Night” has no silent k and “knit” has short i.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people pronounced the k and the gh in “knight”. Today they are silent.

quests.instruction: Which word has an /ar/ sound and a soft c?
quests.hint: Find the word with both an ar and a c that says /s/.
quests.explanation: “Parcel” has ar and a c before e, which says /s/. “Carpet” has a hard c and “party” has no c.

quests.instruction: Which word has a digraph and a long a made by a silent e?
quests.hint: Look for both a digraph and a silent e.
quests.explanation: “Shape” has the digraph sh and the a_e pattern. “Shop” and “chap” have short vowels.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT have a long o sound?
quests.hint: Think about the middle sound of boat and bone. Which word does not match?
quests.explanation: “Boat” and “bone” have long o. “Boot” has the long oo sound.
quests.funFact: Boot has the long oo sound, which is not the same as the long o in boat.

quests.instruction: Which spelling is NOT correct?
quests.hint: Think about how ck and tch show a short vowel.
quests.explanation: “Chek” is not a word. The word “check” ends with ck.

quests.instruction: Which word does NOT have the /k/ sound?
quests.hint: Look at what follows the c in each word.
quests.explanation: “Cell” has a soft c that says /s/. “Cake” and “back” have /k/.

quests.instruction: Which word is read /sh/ /r/ /i/ /m/ /p/?
quests.hint: Match each sound to a letter pattern.
quests.explanation: “Shrimp” is /sh/ /r/ /i/ /m/ /p/. “Shrink” ends with /nk/ and “shrub” has short u.
quests.funFact: Shrimp, shrink and shrub all start with the letters shr.

quests.instruction: Which made-up word would be read with a long i?
quests.hint: Look for a silent e at the end.
quests.explanation: “Pibe” has the i_e pattern, so the i says its name. “Pib” and “pob” have short vowels.

quests.instruction: Which word has five sounds when you count them out?
quests.hint: Count the sounds, not the letters.
quests.explanation: “Stream” is /s/ /t/ /r/ /ē/ /m/, five sounds. “Clean” has 4 and “chain” has 3.
